name: cell-environment-coupling
title: Cell–Environment Coupling (flagship)
question:
When a single cell metabolizes at its own location, does it measurably reshape the very
nutrient gradient it depends on — environmental modification (local resource depletion + secretion) — closing the paper's
§Cell–environment coupling sense → metabolize → secrete loop (Fig 5) as real spatial
metabolism: one cell sensing local glucose, running flux-balance analysis at its own footprint,
growing, and secreting a byproduct that diffuses back into the field it senses? The paper
frames this feedback loop as "the minimal structure required for control"; here the loop is
genuinely closed (a real depletion → uptake feedback), while directed control — chemotaxis up
the sensed gradient — is the deferred half. Mechanistically, the cell and its environment are
two real, independently-built simulators (viva-cpm's Cellular Potts engine, spatio-flux's
diffusion-advection and dynamic-FBA processes) composed through one typed coupling process
(`CpmCellField`), rather than a scripted or lumped stand-in for that coupling.
biological_summary:
A cell does not merely inhabit its environment — it remakes it. Here one
cell sits in a nutrient gradient, eats at its own location, and secretes a byproduct back into
the field, measurably reshaping the very gradient it depends on: environmental modification (local resource depletion + secretion),
realized spatially. This is the paper's §Cell–environment coupling sense → metabolize → secrete
loop (Fig 5), and this investigation's flagship. The paper frames this feedback loop as "the
minimal structure required for control": here the loop is genuinely closed (a real
depletion → uptake feedback), while directed control — chemotaxis up the sensed gradient — is a
tracked, deferred half (see key_assumptions/limitations), so this cell senses, metabolizes,
grows, and secretes, but does not yet act on what it senses. Mechanically it composes two real,
independently-built simulators through one typed coupling process (`CpmCellField`): one CPM cell
— a real Cellular Potts Model agent from viva-cpm, with genuine pixel-level shape, adhesion, and
volume dynamics on a 60x60 lattice — with a shared spatio-flux `fields` grid (glucose, acetate)
running `DiffusionAdvection`. `CpmCellField` is the entire interface between
them: each tick it reads the mean glucose concentration at the cell's current footprint (the
set of lattice pixels the CPM cell occupies), solves one dynamic-FBA step against `e_coli_core`
with Michaelis–Menten-limited glucose uptake (`glucose_km`, `glucose_vmax`) and a fixed
oxygen cap (`oxygen_vmax`) — the O2 cap is what forces the optimizer into mixed-acid acetate
overflow rather than pure aerobic respiration, matching the biological mechanism this coupling
is meant to demonstrate. That causal claim is not left to the code: the O2-uncapped mechanism
control (`o2-cap-forces-acetate-overflow` below) lifts the oxygen bound and shows acetate
secretion collapses to ~0 while the capped flagship secretes a real plume, so the overflow is a
demonstrated experiment rather than an assertion. The coupling then mass-balances the FBA
solution against how much glucose the
footprint actually holds (so the cell can never manufacture biomass or acetate from glucose it
did not actually remove), grows the CPM cell's target volume in proportion to the resulting
biomass, and writes the clamped glucose uptake and acetate secretion back into the field as a
spatial delta. spatio-flux's own `DiffusionAdvection` then spreads both species outward: the
depleted local glucose is partially resupplied from the field's pre-set left-low-to-right-high
gradient, and the secreted acetate forms an expanding plume.

Measured on `single-cell-in-a-field` over 20 ticks (`tests/test_flagship_field.py`,
`tests/test_cpm_cell_field.py`, `tests/test_cpm_viz.py`): the CPM cell grows from 32 to 110
lattice pixels (about 3.4x), against a 60x60 = 3600-pixel lattice — roughly 3% coverage at the
end, nowhere near filling the field. Local footprint glucose peaks at 1.15 (t=2, after diffusion
briefly outpaces the cell's own uptake) then falls to 0.94 by t=20 — ~18% peak-to-trough (the peak
at t=2 is created by diffusion inflow after t=0) and ~6% from the initial condition — as the cell's
own consumption outpaces the partial resupply diffusion provides. Field-wide,
net glucose falls by about 32 units (5940 -> 5908, out of the field's full 3600-pixel total
mass) — a small fraction of the whole field, because only the cell's own footprint and its
immediate diffusive neighborhood are touched, which is exactly the local, footprint-scale
environmental modification the composite is built to show rather than a field-wide depletion event. Acetate,
starting at zero everywhere, rises to a field-wide total of about 47 by t=20 as the secreted
byproduct diffuses into a spreading plume. Biomass (the FBA-tracked internal state driving CPM
growth) rises from 0.1 to about 0.37.
claim:
Composing a real CPM cell with a real spatio-flux nutrient field through one typed
coupling process (`CpmCellField`) reproduces the paper's §Cell–environment coupling
sense → metabolize → secrete loop (Fig 5) as genuine spatial metabolism, not a scripted stand-in
for it (the loop is closed; directed control/chemotaxis is deferred): over 20 ticks the
cell runs dynamic-FBA at its own
footprint (`e_coli_core`, O2-capped to force acetate overflow), grows ~3.4x in CPM volume (32
-> 110 px, ~3% of a 60x60 lattice it does not come close to filling), depletes local glucose by
up to ~18% peak-to-trough (~6% from the initial condition) before diffusion partially resupplies it
(environmental modification), and secretes a
diffusing acetate plume — two independently-built simulators talking through one typed port.

variants.name: mm-mechanism
variants.description:
Interface surrogate-calibration twin (a tuned Michaelis-Menten stand-in — this
investigation's test of the paper's substitutability idea, at the level of surrogate
calibration): the flagship with the cell's INTERNAL metabolism swapped from constraint-based
dynamic-FBA (cobra e_coli_core, O2-capped) to a lumped Michaelis–Menten / Monod metabolism
(`mechanism: mm`, no cobra) BEHIND THE BYTE-IDENTICAL `CpmCellField` ports. Uptake
v = mm_vmax·glc/(mm_km+glc); biomass gain mm_yield·v; acetate overflow mm_overflow·v — a fixed
overflow fraction standing in for the dFBA's O2-cap-driven mixed-acid overflow. The 4 MM params
(mm_vmax 4.0, mm_km 0.5, mm_yield 0.024, mm_overflow 1.4) are TUNED so the interface-level
observables track the dFBA flagship (4 knobs fit to 4 interface observables — exactly determined,
so a good tuned fit is unsurprising); they are not derived from the dFBA solution. The named next
step is now RUN — a genuine held-out test (peer-review M2). With those 4 params FROZEN, dFBA vs MM
was compared on conditions neither was tuned on. Two-sided, honest result — inside the calibrated
glucose-limited, fixed-O2 regime the substitution is mechanism-independent (a different initial
glucose field and a 2x-longer run both hold within ~13%), but the MM box is BLIND to oxygen — on a
held-out O2 cap (dFBA 2.5 -> 5.0) agreement collapses to ~74%, the honest boundary of the swap.

variants.name: steadystate
variants.description: M7d steady-state regime (peer review) — the flagship is a pure transient (no source terms — every flagship claim is a transient reading, never a source/sink equilibrium). This variant adds three cell-INDEPENDENT terms behind the same `CpmCellField` ports so the composite becomes a chemostat-like regime with a genuine flux fixed point — a first-order glucose SOURCE (grid-wide relaxation toward a setpoint, `glucose_source_rate` 0.15 toward `glucose_source_target` 1.5), a first-order acetate DECAY sink (`acetate_decay_rate` 0.2), and a logistic biomass carrying capacity (`biomass_capacity` 0.5) that halts exponential growth at a stationary-phase ceiling. A biomass dilution term alone gives NO interior fixed point in this coupling — the cell's per-pixel uptake scales with biomass/footprint-area (both grow together), so local glucose equilibrates at a biomass-independent value and mu never falls to a dilution rate — the logistic cap is what forces biomass, and hence every flux, to a steady state. Field mass is deliberately NOT conserved here (open-system source/sink); that is the point of a steady state. Run ~120 ticks it reaches a verified steady state (see the `steadystate-flux-equilibrium` acceptance criterion below).

key_assumptions:
e_coli_core constants (`glucose_km` 0.5, `glucose_vmax` 3.5, `oxygen_vmax` 2.5,
`box_volume_L` 0.3, `grow_per_biomass` 300.0) are toy-real: plausible, hand-tuned magnitudes
chosen to produce gradual, spatially-legible dynamics over a short (~20-25 tick) run, not
fitted to a named organism, medium, or literature target.

The metabolized/diffused nutrient field is exclusively the spatio-flux `fields` store
(glucose, acetate) that `CpmCellField` and `DiffusionAdvection` share. The CPM cell's OWN
internal lattice/world (its shape, occupied pixels, footprint) lives inside viva-cpm's Rust
engine as a private object the coupling process owns (`CpmCellField.world`) — it is not a
process-bigraph store, and no other process in the composite reads or writes it. viva-cpm's
own internal field concept (`field_at_cell`, `secretory_types`, `receptor_coupling`) is
separate machinery this composite does not use.

Growth is roughly exponential in this coupling (biomass compounds each tick), so the run is deliberately bounded to ~20-25 ticks — a longer run would need either a saturating growth term or a much larger field to stay spatially legible rather than filling the lattice.

Chemotaxis toward the sensed field (directed up-gradient motion) is deferred to a follow-up variant; the flagship cell senses, metabolizes, grows, and secretes, but does not chemotax — its modest position drift over the run (roughly (17,17) seed to about (18.7, 30.3) by t=20) is CPM thermal fluctuation under the configured temperature, not directed motion.
acceptance_criteria: A cell metabolizing at its footprint should end with more biomass than it started — growth under nutrients.
Under an O2 cap, overflow metabolism should secrete acetate ( > 0 ); lifting the cap should remove that secretion (uncapped acetate ≈ 0).
The metabolizing cell should be a net sink on the shared field — total glucose should fall below its initial value.
Per-species field mass should be conserved — initial mass plus every writer's reported net exchange should equal final mass.

units_and_time.time: 1 tick = unspecified physical time (dimensionless model time); runs are bounded to ~20-25 ticks.
units_and_time.quantities: glucose/acetate field values, biomass, and CPM lattice volume (px) are dimensionless model units. box_volume_L, glucose_km/glucose_vmax and the field concentrations are hand-tuned toy-real magnitudes, not calibrated to mM or to a named medium.

external_anchors: acetate yield under overflow ≈ 0.3-0.5 mol acetate / mol glucose (order-of-magnitude anchor, not a calibration target).
glucose uptake ≈ 10 mmol/gDW/hr (E. coli aerobic) (order-of-magnitude anchor, not a calibration target).

behavior_tests.name: cell-metabolizes-and-grows
behavior_tests.description:
The cell runs dynamic-FBA at its own footprint and grows: biomass rises above its
initial value and CPM volume exceeds 40 px by step 20.

pass_if.provenance: prior: a cell metabolizing at its footprint should end with more biomass than its 0.1 seed (growth under nutrients) → expect final biomass > 0.1. Observed over 20 ticks: biomass 0.1 -> ~0.37 (tests/test_flagship_field.py::test_flagship_sense_act_loop; tests/test_cpm_cell_field.py::test_cell_metabolizes_grows_and_reshapes_field asserts the same pattern on a smaller 40x40 grid over 12 ticks)

behavior_tests.name: cpm-volume-grows
behavior_tests.description: The CPM cell's own target-volume-driven growth carries through to its actual lattice-pixel volume — the cell occupies more pixels by the end of the run.

pass_if.provenance: pin set after the run — CPM volume 32 -> 110 px over 20 ticks (~3.4x), ~3% of the 60x60=3600px lattice; 40 px is a floor above the 32 px seed (tests/test_flagship_field.py::test_flagship_sense_act_loop)

behavior_tests.name: acetate-secreted-and-diffuses
behavior_tests.description: The cell secretes acetate into the shared field as a genuine byproduct of the O2-capped dFBA overflow mechanism, and it is present in the field (i.e. has diffused/spread) by the end of the run.

pass_if.provenance: prior: overflow metabolism under an O2 cap secretes acetate → expect field-wide acetate > 0. Observed: field-wide acetate 0 -> ~47.0 over 20 ticks, spreading into a plume around the cell's footprint (tests/test_flagship_field.py::test_flagship_sense_act_loop; the plume is the third panel of the baked GIF)

behavior_tests.name: net-glucose-consumed
behavior_tests.description: Net field-wide glucose falls over the run — the cell is a genuine sink on the shared field, not merely redistributing it.

pass_if.provenance: prior: a metabolizing cell is a net sink on the shared field → expect total glucose to fall below its 5940.0 initial. Observed: field-wide glucose total 5940.0 -> ~5908.4 over 20 ticks (~32 units net consumed); the local footprint drawdown is much sharper — ~18% peak-to-trough (the peak is created by diffusion inflow after t=0) and ~6% from the initial condition — than the field-wide total, because only the cell's footprint and its immediate diffusive neighborhood are touched (tests/test_flagship_field.py::test_flagship_sense_act_loop)

behavior_tests.name: o2-cap-forces-acetate-overflow
behavior_tests.description: Foundational mechanism control (not this study's scientific claim): the acetate the flagship secretes is CAUSED BY the O2 cap, not an artifact of the coupling. This runs a second composite (`single-cell-in-a-field-o2uncapped`) identical to the flagship except the oxygen bound is lifted (`oxygen_vmax` 2.5 -> 1000, EX_o2_e effectively unbounded). With respiration no longer capacity-limited, unconstrained e_coli_core takes pure aerobic respiration as growth-optimal and EX_ac_e sits at 0 — so the cell secretes ~0 acetate (and grows faster: biomass ~2.35 vs the capped ~0.37), while the capped flagship secretes a real plume. This turns the study's overflow claim ("the O2 cap is what forces the optimizer into mixed-acid overflow") from a code assertion into a demonstrated experiment. The flagship was built first and, unlike the later studies, had no such foundational control until this pass; this is it.

measure.expr: sum(fields.acetate) with oxygen uncapped vs capped

pass_if.provenance: prior: lifting the O2 cap removes the overflow driver, so unconstrained e_coli_core respires fully → expect uncapped acetate ≈ 0. Observed field-wide acetate over 20 ticks: capped flagship 0 -> ~47.0, O2-uncapped 0 -> 0.0 (exactly), a >100x collapse; uncapped biomass ~2.35 vs capped ~0.37 (the cell respires fully instead of overflowing) (tests/test_flagship_field.py::test_o2_cap_is_what_forces_acetate_overflow; composite meta_modelers_guide/composites/single-cell-in-a-field-o2uncapped.composite.json)

behavior_tests.name: field-mass-balance-closes
behavior_tests.description: Foundational conservation control (not this study's scientific claim): the paper frames conservation laws (mass, energy balance) as interface constraints on any coupling. This runs the flagship composite through a closed per-species ledger — for glucose and acetate, initial_field_mass + Σ(every writer's own reported net exchange) == final_field_mass — where the writer's reported delta and what actually accumulates in the shared grid travel through two independent code paths (the process's per-tick arithmetic vs process-bigraph's additive `apply` for a `map[array]` port), so a clamp that manufactures mass, a double-write, or a schema `apply` that concatenates instead of sums surfaces as a nonzero residual. The ledger also shows the cell nets a glucose sink and an acetate source while DiffusionAdvection under Neumann BC nets ~0.

pass_if.provenance: both glucose and acetate ledgers close to < 1e-6 over 15 ticks; cell net glucose < 0 (sink) and net acetate > 0 (source), diff net ~0 for both (tests/test_mass_balance.py::test_flagship_field_mass_balance_closes; meta_modelers_guide/analysis/mass_balance.py)

behavior_tests.name: interface-substitutable-across-mechanisms
behavior_tests.description:
Surrogate calibration of the paper's substitutability idea (the TUNED-condition
baseline for the held-out test below) — a tuned Michaelis-Menten twin (cobra-free) is fit to
reproduce the dFBA flagship's cell↔field interface observables behind the byte-identical
`CpmCellField` ports. The MM twin's 4 free params are TUNED to preserve the interaction variables
(4 knobs fit to 4 observables — exactly determined), so its interface-level observables (final
biomass, total acetate secreted, CPM volume, net glucose depletion) agree with the dFBA flagship
within ~10% on the tuned condition (all four within a 30% tolerance). On its own this is surrogate
calibration — the held-out gate `interface-substitutable-held-out` is what tests independence.

measure.expr: per-observable abs(dFBA - MM) / dFBA over a 20-tick run

pass_if.provenance: over 20 ticks (tests/test_substitutability.py::test_interface_observables_substitutable): biomass dFBA 0.370 vs MM 0.342 (7.5%), CPM volume 110 vs 99 (10%), field-wide acetate 47.02 vs 47.02 (~0%), net glucose depleted 31.6 vs 33.6 (6.2%) — every interface observable within ~10%; the MM path also runs with NO cobra (test_mm_mechanism_runs_without_cobra), the surrogate-model payoff. The 4 MM params (mm_vmax 4.0, mm_km 0.5, mm_yield 0.024, mm_overflow 1.4) were tuned to match (4 knobs fit to 4 observables — exactly determined); the held-out gate below tests them frozen.

behavior_tests.name: interface-substitutable-held-out
behavior_tests.description:
HELD-OUT test of the surrogate (peer-review M2) — the real conversion of surrogate
calibration into a genuine held-out test. The 4 MM params stay FROZEN at their tuned values and
dFBA vs MM are compared on conditions NEITHER was tuned on. Honest two-sided result. Inside the
calibrated glucose-limited, fixed-O2 regime the substitution is mechanism-independent, not just a
fit — on a held-out initial glucose field (flat 3.0, not the tuned 0.3→3.0 gradient) every
interface observable agrees within ~12%, and out to a 2x-longer run (40 ticks) within ~13%. But
the MM box carries no oxygen variable — on a held-out O2 cap (dFBA 2.5→5.0, dFBA-only) agreement
COLLAPSES to ~74% (dFBA nearly quadruples biomass/volume; the O2-blind MM twin cannot follow).
Mechanism-independence holds within the calibrated regime; the O2 axis is the surrogate's blind
spot and the honest boundary of the swap.

measure.expr: per-observable abs(dFBA - MM) / dFBA on held-out conditions, MM params frozen

pass_if.provenance: HELD-OUT, MM params frozen (tests/test_substitutability_heldout.py). GATE — held-out glucose field flat 3.0 over 20 ticks — biomass dFBA 0.531 vs MM 0.480 (9.7%), CPM volume 160 vs 141 (11.9%), acetate 74.9 vs 73.8 (1.4%), net glucose depleted 49.1 vs 52.7 (7.3%) — worst 11.9%, within the 0.15 band (::test_heldout_glucose_field_substitutable). CORROBORATION — 40-tick run — biomass 1.282 vs 1.123 (12.4%), volume 383 vs 335 (12.5%), acetate 207 vs 199 (4.1%), glucose 139 vs 142 (2.0%) — worst 12.5% (::test_heldout_longer_run_substitutable). BOUNDARY (diagnostic, not gated small) — held-out O2 cap 2.5→5.0 diverges 73-74% on biomass/volume (dFBA 1.282/382 vs frozen MM 0.342/99): the surrogate is blind to O2 (::test_surrogate_is_blind_to_oxygen_heldout). Degrees of freedom — 4 free MM params vs 4 interface observables (exactly determined), so the tuned fit was guaranteed; the held-out agreement in-regime is the real evidence.

behavior_tests.name: steadystate-flux-equilibrium
behavior_tests.description: M7d steady-state check (peer review) — the flagship is a pure transient with no source terms, so every flagship number is a transient reading, never a source/sink equilibrium. The `single-cell-in-a-field-steadystate` variant adds a first-order glucose source, a first-order acetate decay sink, and a logistic biomass carrying capacity, and is run ~120 ticks to a VERIFIED flux steady state — d(biomass)/dt and both field fluxes fall below tolerance while the cell keeps metabolizing at maintenance. This answers the limitation the flagship itself flags (the field has no continuous source or decay term).

measure.expr: max per-tick relative change of biomass and of each field total over the final 10 of 120 ticks

pass_if.provenance: STEADY STATE REACHED. Criterion — over the final 10 of 120 ticks the max per-tick relative change of biomass and of both field totals is < 0.1%. Measured (tests/test_flagship_field.py::test_steadystate_regime_reaches_flux_steady_state) — biomass 0.0015%/tick, field glucose 0.0001%/tick, field acetate 0.014%/tick, all three below the 0.1% tolerance. Standing steady-state values — biomass ~0.500 (the biomass_capacity ceiling), CPM volume ~147 px (stable to CPM thermal noise ~3 px), local footprint glucose ~1.356, field glucose total ~5372 (uptake balanced by source), field acetate total ~31.5 (secretion balanced by decay). The cell is alive and metabolizing at the fixed point, not a dead/zeroed field.

behavior_tests.name: cadence-convergence
behavior_tests.description: M7d cadence rigor check (peer review) — the flagship's operator-split CPM<->dFBA<->diffusion loop runs at coupling cadence 1, and only the PDE substeps are CFL-guarded today. Halving then quartering the coupling cadence (sub-step interval 1 -> 0.5 -> 0.25) and measuring the drift in the four gated observables between the two finest levels tests whether the pinned trajectories are cadence-converged. Convergence band is <= 10%. HONEST two-sided result — the three TIME-INTEGRATED gated observables converge tightly, but the INSTANTANEOUS local-footprint glucose does NOT (it is the one pinned trajectory that moves under refinement, flagged on F-02 below).

measure.expr: abs(drift) between coupling cadence 0.25 and 0.5 (finest two levels), per observable

pass_if.provenance: MEASURED drift between the finest two cadences (0.25 vs 0.5), deterministic fixed-seed run (tests/test_flagship_field.py::test_flagship_cadence_convergence). CONVERGED within the 10% band — final biomass 1.6%, CPM volume 2.6%, net glucose depleted 1.8%, field-wide acetate 1.7% (values — biomass 0.375 vs 0.381, volume 111 vs 114, net glucose 32.3 vs 32.9, acetate 48.1 vs 49.0). NOT CONVERGED — the instantaneous local-footprint glucose (obs.local_nutrient) drifts 15.7% (0.864 vs 1.025), EXCEEDING the band, because it is a single-tick snapshot over a stochastically-shifting CPM footprint and the CPM's fixed mcs_per_update is NOT interval-scaled (halving the cadence doubles the total Monte-Carlo relaxation the lattice receives). Finding — the integrated flagship claims (biomass/volume growth, acetate plume, net glucose sink) are cadence-robust; the local-depletion pin (F-02's 0.94 / ~18% peak-to-trough / ~6% from initial) is cadence-sensitive and is re-levelled to an approximate, not cadence-converged, reading.

findings.statement:
A real CPM cell coupled to a real spatio-flux nutrient field through one typed
process (`CpmCellField`) closes the paper's §Cell–environment coupling
sense → metabolize → secrete loop (Fig 5) as genuine spatial metabolism (the loop is closed;
directed control/chemotaxis is deferred): it
runs dynamic-FBA at its own footprint and grows both biologically (biomass) and structurally
(CPM lattice volume). Confirmed: biomass 0.1 -> ~0.37, CPM volume 32 -> 110 px (~3.4x) over
20 ticks, on a 3600-pixel lattice the cell occupies only ~3% of by the end.

The cell measurably depletes the local nutrient it senses before diffusion partially
resupplies it — environmental modification as a direct spatial-metabolic consequence, not a scripted
trajectory. Confirmed: local footprint glucose concentration peaks at 1.15 (t=2) and falls to
0.94 by t=20 — ~18% peak-to-trough (the peak is created by diffusion inflow after t=0) and ~6%
from the initial condition — while the field-wide glucose total falls by only
~32 of 5940 units — the depletion signature is sharply local to the cell's own footprint and
its immediate diffusive neighborhood, not a field-wide event.

CADENCE CAVEAT (M7d re-level) — the QUALITATIVE finding (a sharply-local depletion halo,
net field-wide sink) is cadence-robust, and the field-wide net-consumption number (~32 units)
is cadence-converged (< 2% drift under cadence halving, see `cadence-convergence`). But the
INSTANTANEOUS local-footprint figures quoted here — the 0.94 endpoint, the ~18% peak-to-trough
and ~6%-from-initial depths — are NOT cadence-converged — the local footprint concentration is
a single-tick snapshot over a stochastically-shifting CPM footprint (whose fixed mcs_per_update
is not interval-scaled), and it drifts ~16% between coupling cadence 0.25 and 0.5. These local
depths are therefore APPROXIMATE, cadence-1 readings, not converged quantities; the load-bearing
claim (local depletion happens and is sharply local) stands.

evidence.observed: local footprint glucose 1.15 -> 0.94 (~18% peak-to-trough, ~6% from initial — approximate, NOT cadence-converged — see cadence-convergence, ~16% drift under cadence halving); field-wide glucose 5940.0 -> ~5908.4 (net consumption cadence-converged < 2%)

findings.statement:
The O2-capped dynamic-FBA mechanism forces the optimizer into mixed-acid acetate
overflow (rather than pure aerobic respiration), and that byproduct genuinely diffuses
outward into a spreading plume via spatio-flux's own `DiffusionAdvection` process — the
secretion side of the coupling is as real as the uptake side. Confirmed: field-wide acetate
0 -> ~47.0 over 20 ticks.

The acetate overflow is CAUSED BY the O2 cap, shown by experiment rather than
asserted from code: lifting the oxygen bound (O2-uncapped control, oxygen_vmax 2.5 -> 1000)
collapses acetate secretion to ~0 while the capped flagship secretes a real plume — the cell
respires fully instead of overflowing (and grows faster for it). Confirmed: field-wide acetate
capped 0 -> ~47.0 vs uncapped 0 -> 0.0 (exactly); uncapped biomass ~2.35 vs capped ~0.37.

evidence.observed: acetate capped ~47.0 vs uncapped 0.0; biomass uncapped ~2.35 vs capped ~0.37

findings.statement:
INTERFACE SURROGATE CALIBRATION — a tuned Michaelis-Menten twin reproduces the
flagship's cell↔field interface observables, this investigation's test of the paper's
substitutability idea at the level of surrogate calibration. The paper (§2 / §Cellular interface)
argues that "this substitutability is not only a
software convenience. It allows the interface itself to become the object of comparison:
different mechanisms may realize the same externally observable relation", and that "different
internal organizations may sometimes be represented through the same coarse-grained interface
when they preserve the interaction variables relevant to that description." Here that idea is
put to a first test: the flagship cell's INTERNAL metabolism is swapped from constraint-based
dynamic-FBA (cobra e_coli_core, O2-capped) to a lumped, cobra-free Michaelis–Menten / Monod metabolism
(`single-cell-in-a-field-mm`, `mechanism: mm`) behind the BYTE-IDENTICAL `CpmCellField` ports,
and the interface-level observables are compared head-to-head. Confirmed: over 20 ticks the tuned
MM twin reproduces the coarse-grained cell↔field interface — final
biomass dFBA 0.370 vs MM 0.342 (7.5%), CPM volume 110 vs 99 px (10%), total acetate secreted
47.02 vs 47.02 (~0%), net glucose depleted 31.6 vs 33.6 units (6.2%); every interface observable
agrees within ~10%. The MM twin additionally runs with NO cobra at all — the surrogate-model
payoff, a mechanism that runs where the original could not. This is surrogate calibration, not yet
mechanism-independence: the 4 MM params
(mm_vmax 4.0, mm_km 0.5, mm_yield 0.024, mm_overflow 1.4) were TUNED to preserve the interaction
variables (4 knobs fit to 4 observables — exactly determined) — the claim is "a tuned surrogate
matches the coarse-grained relation", not identical internals, and not a derivation of MM from the
dFBA solution.

HELD-OUT TEST NOW RUN (peer-review M2) — the named next step is done, and re-levels this finding
honestly on both sides. With the 4 MM params FROZEN at their tuned values, dFBA vs MM were compared
on conditions neither was tuned on (tests/test_substitutability_heldout.py). Inside the calibrated
glucose-limited, fixed-O2 regime the substitution is MECHANISM-INDEPENDENT, not just a fit — a
held-out initial glucose field (flat 3.0, not the tuned 0.3→3.0 gradient) agrees within 11.9% on
every observable, and a 2x-longer run (40 ticks) within 12.5%. But the lumped MM box carries NO
oxygen variable, and that is its blind spot — on a held-out O2 cap (dFBA 2.5→5.0) dFBA nearly
quadruples its biomass/volume while the O2-blind MM twin is unchanged, so agreement COLLAPSES to
~74%. The honest re-level — mechanism-independence WITHIN the calibrated regime (held-out within
~13% on the glucose/time axes), surrogate calibration only ACROSS the O2 axis the MM box has no
variable for. Degrees of freedom — 4 free MM params vs 4 interface observables (exactly determined),
so the tuned fit was guaranteed a priori; the in-regime held-out agreement is the load-bearing
evidence, and the O2-axis collapse is the load-bearing limitation.

evidence.observed: TUNED (20 ticks): biomass 0.370 vs 0.342 (7.5%), volume 110 vs 99 (10%), acetate 47.02 vs 47.02 (~0%), glucose 31.6 vs 33.6 (6.2%). HELD-OUT frozen: flat-3.0 field within 11.9%, 40-tick within 12.5%; held-out O2 cap 2.5→5.0 diverges ~74% (MM blind to O2). MM runs cobra-free

findings.statement: STEADY-STATE REGIME (M7d, peer review) — the flagship is a pure transient (no source terms), so every flagship number is a transient reading, never a source/sink equilibrium, and the study itself flags this as a limitation. Adding three cell-independent terms behind the same `CpmCellField` ports — a first-order glucose source (grid-wide relaxation toward a setpoint), a first-order acetate decay sink, and a logistic biomass carrying capacity — turns the composite into a chemostat-like regime that reaches a VERIFIED flux steady state. Confirmed — over the final 10 of 120 ticks the per-tick relative change of biomass (0.0015%), field glucose (0.0001%), and field acetate (0.014%) all fall below the 0.1% steady-state tolerance, with standing values biomass ~0.500, CPM volume ~147 px, local glucose ~1.356, field glucose ~5372 (uptake balanced by source), field acetate ~31.5 (secretion balanced by decay); the cell is alive and metabolizing at the fixed point. Note — a biomass dilution term alone gives NO interior fixed point in this coupling (per-pixel uptake scales with biomass/footprint-area, so local glucose equilibrates biomass-independently and mu never falls to a dilution rate); the logistic carrying capacity is what forces every flux to a steady state. This demonstrates the source/sink-equilibrium regime the flagship deferred.

evidence.observed: per-tick relative flux < 0.1% over the final 10 of 120 ticks (biomass 0.0015%, glucose 0.0001%, acetate 0.014%); standing values biomass ~0.500, volume ~147 px, local glucose ~1.356, field glucose ~5372, field acetate ~31.5

findings.statement: CADENCE CONVERGENCE (M7d, peer review) — the flagship's operator-split CPM<->dFBA<->diffusion loop runs at coupling cadence 1, and only the PDE substeps are CFL-guarded. Halving then quartering the coupling cadence and measuring the drift in the four gated observables between the two finest levels gives an HONEST two-sided result. The three TIME-INTEGRATED gated observables are cadence-robust — between cadence 0.25 and 0.5 final biomass drifts 1.6%, CPM volume 2.6%, net glucose depleted 1.8%, and field-wide acetate 1.7%, all inside the 10% convergence band. But the INSTANTANEOUS local-footprint glucose does NOT converge — it drifts 15.7% (0.864 vs 1.025), exceeding the band, because it is a single-tick snapshot over a stochastically-shifting CPM footprint and the CPM's fixed mcs_per_update is not interval-scaled (halving the cadence doubles the total Monte-Carlo relaxation the lattice receives). Re-level — the integrated flagship claims (biomass/volume growth, acetate plume, net glucose sink) are cadence-converged and stand as-is; F-02's LOCAL-DEPLETION pin (the 0.94 endpoint, ~18% peak-to-trough, ~6%-from-initial depths) is cadence-sensitive and is re-levelled to an approximate, cadence-1 reading — the one pinned trajectory the cadence check moves.

evidence.observed: drift between finest two cadences (0.25 vs 0.5) — biomass 1.6%, volume 2.6%, net glucose 1.8%, acetate 1.7% (all < 10% band); local-footprint glucose 15.7% (exceeds band — NOT converged)

regression_compatibility.basis: single-cell-in-a-field.composite.json (and its O2-uncapped control sibling single-cell-in-a-field-o2uncapped.composite.json) build and run to completion through the process-bigraph engine (tests/test_flagship_field.py, tests/test_cpm_cell_field.py, tests/test_cpm_viz.py, tests/test_mass_balance.py, tests/test_composites_build.py); guarded skip when the optional cobra dependency is absent, matching this investigation's FBA-grain convention.

biological_validation.basis: All four primary behavior tests pass on measured readouts from a real 20-tick run — the cell metabolizes and grows (biomass, CPM volume), depletes its own local nutrient before diffusion resupplies it (environmental modification), and secretes a diffusing acetate plume — and the two foundational controls hold. The O2-uncapped control demonstrates the overflow is caused by the O2 cap (uncapped acetate ~0), and the closed field mass-balance ledger closes to < 1e-6 for glucose and acetate.

explanatory_gain.basis: Composing a real Cellular Potts cell with a real spatial dFBA+diffusion simulator through one typed process makes the paper's cell-environment coupling claim concrete at a level of mechanistic resolution a coarser, lumped 9-cell grid could not reach — genuine cell shape, genuine flux-balance optimization, genuine PDE diffusion, all talking through one interface neither framework was built with the other in mind for.

conclusion:
## Claims
- A single cell reshapes the very nutrient gradient it depends on — environmental modification
(local resource depletion + secretion), realized spatially. Composing a real CPM cell with a real spatio-flux nutrient
field through one typed coupling process (`CpmCellField`) reproduces the paper's
§Cell–environment coupling sense → metabolize → secrete loop (Fig 5) as genuine spatial
metabolism — the loop closed (depletion → uptake feedback), with directed control (chemotaxis)
the deferred half.
Over 20 ticks the cell grows ~3.4x in CPM volume (32 -> 110 px, ~3% of a 60x60 lattice it does
not come close to filling), depletes its own local glucose by ~18% peak-to-trough (~6% from the
initial condition) before diffusion partially resupplies it (environmental modification), and
secretes a diffusing acetate plume from an
O2-capped dynamic-FBA overflow mechanism.

## Evidence
- **CELL-METABOLIZES-AND-GROWS** — biomass 0.1 -> ~0.37 via dynamic-FBA at the cell's own
footprint
- **CPM-VOLUME-GROWS** — CPM lattice volume 32 -> 110 px (~3.4x), ~3% lattice coverage
- **ACETATE-SECRETED-AND-DIFFUSES** — field-wide acetate 0 -> ~47.0 as the plume spreads
- **NET-GLUCOSE-CONSUMED** — field-wide glucose 5940.0 -> ~5908.4; local footprint drawdown
~18% peak-to-trough (~6% from initial)
- **O2-CAP-FORCES-ACETATE-OVERFLOW** (foundational control) — O2-uncapped acetate 0 -> 0.0
(exactly) vs capped 0 -> ~47.0: the overflow is caused by the O2 cap, shown by experiment
- **FIELD-MASS-BALANCE-CLOSES** (foundational control) — glucose and acetate ledgers close to
< 1e-6 (cell nets a glucose sink + acetate source; diffusion nets ~0)

## Limitations
- e_coli_core constants (`glucose_km`, `glucose_vmax`, `oxygen_vmax`, `box_volume_L`,
`grow_per_biomass`) are toy-real — plausible, hand-tuned magnitudes, not fitted to any
organism or medium.
- Chemotaxis toward the sensed field is deferred to a follow-up variant; the cell does not move
directionally up-gradient in this composite. Its modest position drift is CPM thermal
fluctuation, not directed motion.
- Growth is roughly exponential in this coupling, so the run is deliberately bounded to
~20-25 ticks to stay spatially legible; a longer run was not attempted.
- The metabolized field is exclusively the spatio-flux `fields` store; the CPM cell's own
internal lattice/world is a private, write-protected object inside viva-cpm's Rust engine,
not a process-bigraph store, and no other process reads or writes it.
## Next steps
- Add directed chemotaxis (motion up the sensed gradient) as a variant of this composite.
- Multi-cell competition over one shared field is realized in `cell-cell-coupling`, which reuses
`CpmCellField` for each competing cell.

local footprint glucose never depletes despite consumption (mass-balance/clamp bug)
acetate never appears in the field (O2 cap not forcing overflow, or the secretion write is not reaching the shared field store)

limitations: e_coli_core constants (glucose_km, glucose_vmax, oxygen_vmax, box_volume_L, grow_per_biomass) are toy-real, hand-tuned magnitudes chosen for gradual, legible dynamics over a short run — not fitted to any organism or medium.

Chemotaxis toward the external field is deferred to a follow-up variant; the cell senses, metabolizes, grows, and secretes, but does not move directionally up-gradient. The minimal extension is well understood — bias the CPM target/footprint up the local gradient (a toy 1-D gradient-drift rule) — so directed action is a small increment, not a new mechanism.
Growth is roughly exponential in this coupling, so the run is deliberately bounded to ~20-25 ticks to stay spatially legible.

The metabolized nutrient field is exclusively the spatio-flux ``fields`` store; the CPM cell's own internal lattice/world lives inside viva-cpm's Rust engine as a private, write-protected object the coupling process owns, not a process-bigraph store — no other process in the composite reads or writes it, and viva-cpm's own internal field concept (field_at_cell/secretory_types) is separate machinery this composite does not use.

The cell's only channel for acting back on its environment here is metabolic (uptake and secretion). A second, non-metabolic sense/act channel — mechanical stress / traction, where the cell pushes on its surroundings and reads the reaction force — is not modeled; it is a candidate future coupling process alongside chemotaxis.

The FLAGSHIP nutrient field has no continuous source or decay term — its 20-tick dynamics are transient depletion plus diffusion, not a source/sink equilibrium. M7d (peer review) now ADDRESSES this — the `single-cell-in-a-field-steadystate` variant adds a first-order glucose source, a first-order acetate decay sink, and a logistic biomass carrying capacity, and reaches a verified flux steady state by ~t=100-120 (finding F-06). The flagship itself remains a transient by design; the steady-state regime is the standing-field extension.

CADENCE (M7d, peer review) — the operator-split CPM<->dFBA<->diffusion loop runs at coupling cadence 1 and only the PDE substeps are CFL-guarded. A cadence-halving/quartering convergence check (finding F-07) shows the time-integrated gated observables (biomass/volume growth, acetate plume, net glucose sink) are cadence-converged (< 3% drift between cadence 0.25 and 0.5), but the INSTANTANEOUS local-footprint glucose is NOT (~16% drift) because the CPM's fixed mcs_per_update is not interval-scaled. F-02's local-depletion depths (0.94 / ~18% / ~6%) are therefore approximate cadence-1 readings, not converged quantities; a cadence-invariant local reading would require interval-scaling the CPM Monte-Carlo sweeps, a follow-up.
falsifiability: Overturned if the cell's biomass or CPM lattice volume never rise over the run, if local footprint glucose never depletes despite ongoing consumption, if acetate never appears in the shared field (the O2 cap failing to force overflow, or the secretion write not reaching the field store), or if net field-wide glucose does not fall (the cell failing to act as a genuine sink on the shared field).
